sentences.text:
This Crl.M.C has beel filed to quash all further proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.1868/2021 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kodungallur (for short 'the court below').
2.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kodungallur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is the accused No.3.
The 2nd respondent is the de facto complainant.
The 1 st accused is the husband and the 2nd accused is the mother in law of the 2nd respondent.

3. The offences alleged against the petitioner are punishable under Sections 323, 498A and 506(i)
r/w Section 34 of IPC.

4. I have heard Smt.Dhanya P.Ashokan, the learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri.P.K.Varghese, the learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent as well as Sri.Sangeetha Raj, the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. The learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that even if the entire allegations in the first information statement together with the materials collected during investigation are believed in toto, no offences under Sections 323, 498A and 506(i) of IPC are attracted against the petitioner.

Per contra, the learned counsel for the 2nd respondent submitted that there are sufficient allegations to attract the offence against the petitioner and when prima facie case is made out, the jurisdiction vested with this Court under Section 482 of Cr.P.C cannot be invoked.
6. The crime was registered on the basis of a private complaint.
Annexure I is the certified copy of the private complaint.
The private complaint was forwarded to the police for investigation under Section 156(3) of Cr.P.C and thereafter the crime was registered.
After investigation, the final report was filed.
Annexure III is the copy of the final report.

Annexure IV is the copy of the statement of the 2 nd respondent recorded by the police during investigation under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
7.
The marriage was solemnized on 28.3.2002.
The private complaint was filed after 19 years of the marriage ie. in the year 2021.
The specific allegation against the petitioner has been stated in para 2 of Annexure I.

The allegation is that within a year of the marriage, the petitioner came to the house of the 1 st accused, where he along with the 2nd respondent were residing, for her delivery and at that time she exercised mental cruelty stating that the gold ornaments given to the 2nd respondent by her parents were less than what was given to her by her parents.
There is no specific allegation of demanding dowry so as to attract Section 498A of IPC.
That apart, the said incident took place in the year 2003.
Till 2021, there was no complaint.

Apart from the above allegation, there is a general allegation against all the accused that all of them subjected the 2nd respondent to cruelty demanding more dowry, but there is no specific allegation against the petitioner.

8. The Apex Court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of Section 498A of IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes and Sandhya vs State Of Kerala on 18 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156183418/
2 warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them.
(See Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar (AIR 2022 SC 820) and K.Subba Rao v. State of Telangana [(2018) 14 SCC 452].

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar (AIR 2022 SC 820)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: K.Subba Rao v. State of Telangana [(2018) 14 SCC 452]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In K. Subba Rao (Supra), the Apex Court held that the court should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.
It was further held that the relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.
In Kahkashan Kausar (supra), it was held that in the absence of any specific role attributed to the in-laws, it would be unjust if they are forced to go through the tribulations of trial.

It was further held that the allegations that are general and omnibus do not warrant prosecution under Section 498A of IPC.
9.

Apart from the general and omnibus allegation against the petitioner, that too something which took place 18 years prior to the filing of the private complaint, there are no specific allegation against the petitioner.
For the reasons stated above, I am of the view that no purpose will be served in proceeding against the petitioner.
Hence, all further proceedings against the petitioner in C.C.No.1868/2021 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Kodungallur is hereby quashed.
